outcome: The one result found that is a genuine case-reduction of the exact stated conjecture (char-0 implies positive-characteristic, Izquierdo & Lucchini Arteche) was first posted to arXiv on 2023-08-02, before the frozen revision. Its only post-window developments are a 2025 arXiv text revision and 2025 journal publication with no new mathematical content. No other post-window source narrows the conjecture's remaining open cases (anisotropic E6/E7/E8, trialitarian D4 over imperfect fields), and no AI system was involved anywhere in this line of work.
summary: The most relevant work I found on Serre's conjecture II as stated (simply connected semisimple groups over perfect fields of cohomological dimension ≤ 2) is Izquierdo & Lucchini Arteche's 'Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II' (arXiv 2308.00903), which proves that the conjecture in characteristic 0 implies it in positive characteristic. Under §3.1 this is a genuine case-reduction of the exact stated conjecture (it restricts by field characteristic, it does not change the statement), so it would qualify as `partial` if dated within the window. But per §6.3, the event is dated by the first public written argument, and arXiv v1 was submitted 2023-08-02 — about 5.5 months before the frozen revision's 2024-01-26 timestamp. The only things that happened to this paper after the freeze are a v2 revision (2023-12-14, still pre-window), a v3 revision (2025-09-09), and journal publication in Advances in Mathematics vol. 480 (Nov 2025). I checked the abstract and available text of v3 against v1/v2 and found no indication of new theorems, expanded case coverage, or a different proof technique — it reads as the same pre-window result carried through peer review, and §6.3 explicitly excludes journal-publication lag from counting as new movement. I therefore classify this as `open_stale`: the qualifying event predates the frozen revision and nothing found afterward changes the mathematics. Two other post-window items exist but do not bear on this bullet: (1) arXiv 2603.08061 (Nguyen, 2026-03-09) generalizes Serre's conjecture II to the strictly broader class of pseudo-reductive groups and proves an equivalence there — this changes the statement of a different (broader) question rather than settling a case of the one stated (simply connected semisimple groups), so under §3.1 it is a related/variant problem, not a case; (2) arXiv 2312.10442 (Bingöl & Quéguiner-Mathieu, v1 2023-12-16, v2 2025-11-02) constructs anisotropic trialitarian D4 triples, relevant background to the still-open D4-over-imperfect-fields case, but v1 predates the window and the 2025 v2 update appears to be a journal-acceptance revision with no resolution of the open case. Current Wikipedia's live article confirms the conjecture remains open for anisotropic E6, E7, E8 and trialitarian D4 over imperfect fields, with no post-2024 resolution reported. No source found — papers, journal metadata, or secondary coverage — mentions any AI or machine-learning system in connection with any of this work; it is all conventional human mathematics, so `ai_role` is `none`.
competing_reading: One could argue the September 2025 arXiv revision and November 2025 journal publication constitute the case-reduction result becoming citable/authoritative within the window, and that a looser reading of 'first public written argument' could use the v3 date since that is the version experts now cite. I disfavor this because §6.3 is explicit that journal-publication lag (and, by the same logic, a non-substantive text revision) should not be substituted for the true first-appearance date, precisely to prevent stale pre-window work from re-entering as new movement. If a downstream reviewer determines v3 does contain materially new content not in v1/v2, this record should be revised toward `partial` dated to 2025-09-09.
what_would_settle_it: A full-text diff of arXiv 2308.00903 v1 vs v3 (I could only access abstract/metadata-level summaries of each) to confirm with certainty that no new theorem, case, or strengthened bound was added in the 2025 revision.
